label: November 2–8
title: “A New Spirit Will I Put within You” —  Ezekiel 1–3; 33–34; 36

items.text: Even in exile, far from the temple, Ezekiel saw the glory of the Lord among the captives. This vision reminds us that God’s presence can be found even in our darkest moments, and His love extends to all His children, regardless of their circumstances.

Despite the wickedness of the people, God had not abandoned them. He promised that if they would 'hear the word of the Lord,' what was once dead could be revived. Our 'stony hearts' can be replaced with 'new hearts,' offering hope for spiritual renewal.

The Lord called leaders 'watchmen' and 'shepherds,' inviting us to care for His sheep. This sacred calling requires us to feed, guide, and protect those entrusted to us, following the Savior’s example as our ultimate Shepherd.
The Lord desires to forgive. He teaches us about repentance, not trusting in our own righteousness, but in His boundless mercy. When we turn to Him, He offers a path to forgiveness and a clean heart.

The vision of dry bones coming to life symbolizes the gathering of Israel. The Lord is actively bringing His scattered children back to Him, both on this earth and on the other side of the veil, restoring them to spiritual life.

The joining of the stick of Judah (the Bible) and the stick of Joseph (the Book of Mormon) signifies the powerful role of scriptures in gathering Israel. These sacred texts work together to help us come unto Christ.
The Lord promised a new temple and a new Jerusalem, where His name would be honored. This prophecy points to a future of restored righteousness and the enduring presence of the Lord among His people.

Ezekiel’s call to prophesy to a rebellious house reveals the difficult but necessary work of bearing testimony. Despite the challenges, we are invited to share the Lord’s word with conviction and compassion.
The imagery of good pasture and a secure fold represents the blessings of the gospel and the safety found within the Lord’s covenant. He provides for us and protects us when we follow Him.

The Lord's desire is to restore His people. He promises to cleanse them from their iniquities, give them a new spirit, and lead them to a land of promise, demonstrating His unwavering love and commitment to their salvation.
